transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 15:30 UTC (7:30 PT)
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (QuantaHealth), Eric Cho (QuantaHealth), Sofia Alvarez (QuantaHealth)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): finalize go-live guardrails, agree on traffic ramp plan, finalize runbook and dry-run schedule.

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're running a little behind schedule so i'll kick us off, quick roll call?
[00:10] Maya: maya here, hi.
[00:12] Eric: eric, platform.
[00:14] Sofia: sofia, s r e.
[00:16] Carlos: carlos, se at redwood.
[00:18] Aisha: awesome, cool. quick agenda, results from the last week's soak, guard rails for cutover, monitor/alerts, runbook edits, and then next steps / dry run scheduling. sound good?
[00:28] Maya: yeah sounds good. we did a 48 hour soak at 5% traffic, we saw an uptick in tail latency around request 150k mark, like 95th jumped from 180 to 420 ms, so want to validate the mitigation options you suggested.
[00:44] Carlos: ok yeah that's helpful; i looked at the traces — there's a pattern where batching spikes while kv cache warmup happens. in our runtime we saw contiguous requests with long sequences causing the batching coalescer to back up. might be weighty for the GPU mem allocator. we talked about decreasing max batch size and enabling prefix caching.
[01:04] Sofia: small note — some transcriptions call it K V cache and others K V cache spelled out, but it's the same. also the SLO you guys have is aggressive for our p99.
[01:14] Aisha: right. so proposal for canary: a staged ramp. start 5% -> 15% -> 30% over three business-hour windows with SLO/alert gates at each step. if any gate trips, auto-fallback to previous percent and open an incident.
[01:30] Eric: what's the trip criteria exactly? is it p95 or p99 latency, error rate, and a quality gate?
[01:36] Carlos: we recommend combined: 3 things — error rate > 0.5% sustained for 3 minutes, p99 latency increase > 2x baseline for 5 minutes, or quality regression measured by the eval set where BLEU-like score drops by >= 8%. we can tweak thresholds based on your metrics.
[01:58] Maya: the quality gate is the tricky part — our end-user examples matter more than avg metrics. we'll provide a small prioritized prompt set, about 200 items, can you run it through the canary path?
[02:10] Carlos: yes, we'll run the prompt set before each ramp step as a smoke, and we'll compare to baseline. note: model variance and sampling seeds can introduce noise — we can set a noise tolerance.
[02:24] Aisha: okay so runbook callouts: 1) pre-ramp smoke run of 200 prompts, 2) telemetry check (token counters, p50/p95/p99, error rate), 3) KV cache warmup observation window 10 minutes, 4) rollback criteria and escalations. we'll include these in runbook v2.
[02:44] Sofia: can we add a control-plane fallback? like if redwood's dedicated pool is constrained, route to the hosted fallback with redaction? we need a plan for data residency and PII redaction.
[02:56] Carlos: absolutely — we support policy-based routing. fallback options are: A) compatible quantized variant in same region, B) hosted fallback (with stricter logging), C) degrade to shorter max tokens to reduce mem pressure. each option has tradeoffs on cost and data handling.
[03:14] Eric: on the hosted fallback, how are audit logs handled — do they show customer ids? we need to ensure KMS/HSM keys are used for envelopes and that logs are scrubbed.
[03:24] Aisha: we have an SSO/KMS integration doc; in the private deployment the customer manages the KMS. hosted fallback will keep minimal metadata and we can toggle audit verbosity. we'll share the security cookbook link after the call.
[03:38] Maya: also SOC2 questions — will your audit logs be acceptable for our compliance team if we go hybrid?
[03:44] Aisha: yes, we can provide SOC2 attestation and full audit log samples; for hybrid we'll provide remote-writing of audit events to your splunk/s3 via dedicated connectors.
[03:54] Carlos: back to telemetry: we propose a canary dashboard with the following panels: error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, cpu/gpu utilization, KV cache hit rate, token counts and a small diff panel for the quality eval. we'll set alerts for each.
[04:14] Sofia: what's the expected alert cadence? we want to avoid alert fatigue during ramp.
[04:18] Carlos: good point — alerts should be aggregated and use burn-rate style thresholds, e.g., p99 spikes for >5 minutes triggers a P0, but transient blips under 90s are warnings only. we can also set alerted-on-call-only for the first ramp.
[04:34] Maya: how about traffic slicing — we want to split traffic by user cohort for A/B. would redwood support percentage assignment by header or by cookie?
[04:42] Carlos: yes, routing supports both header-based and hashed user-id slicing. you can define cohorts and we can orchestrate a/b with parallel model endpoints. note: running two model variants doubles cost for sampled traffic.
[04:56] Eric: budget concerns, yes. can we gate A/B to only 2% traffic for the first week?
[04:59] Aisha: absolutely. recommended path: do the progressive ramp on the primary variant first, then if stable, spin up A/B at 2% for an overnight steady-state.
[05:10] Maya: and rollback — do we do an automatic rollback to previous weight or full cut to 0%?
[05:14] Carlos: auto-fallback will step back to the last safe weight (e.g., 30% -> 15%) and pause the ramp. operator can then choose full cut. full cut is last-resort and should be defined in runbook.
[05:26] Sofia: can you add a fast-cut path in the control plane for emergency, like kill-switch route that changes routing in less than 30s?
[05:33] Carlos: yes, the control plane supports an emergency kill switch. it can be RBAC protected and require two confirmations. we'll include an example in runbook.
[05:44] Aisha: we're nearing the safety window conversation — your team suggested 9–11am PT next Tuesday for a dry-run, does that still work?
[05:51] Maya: yeah that's fine.
[05:53] Eric: works for us, platform will be available.
[05:55] Aisha: great. we'll do a dry-run of the runbook: pre-smoke, 5->15% ramp for 30m, validate, then rollback. no external traffic shift, this is internal sampling only.
[06:08] Maya: one ask — in the dry-run please simulate error injection so we can validate alerting and on-call response.
[06:14] Carlos: ok we can simulate 502s and high latency by toggling a fault injection flag on the test pool. we'll coordinate test windows with sofia.
[06:24] Sofia: i'll be on-call for that window and will own incident creation.
[06:28] Eric: on the quality eval side, maya will upload the 200 prompt set to the shared drive, what's the format?
[06:35] Maya: csv with id, prompt, expected_behaviour, priority. we'll also annotate which responses are safety-critical.
[06:42] Carlos: perfect. we'll run the set and produce a diff report. note the eval harness is noisy; we'll include random seeds and run three passes.
[06:53] Aisha: any outstanding legal/procurement checks before the dry-run?
[06:56] Eric: procurement wants final pricing for the pilot capacity; we have an internal sign-off threshold. can you share the pilot pricing sheet and assumptions?
[07:03] Aisha: yes i'll send the pilot pricing spreadsheet and a short note on assumptions today.
[07:10] Maya: ai infra question — if we enable quantization to reduce memory, what's the expected delta on quality? we've seen 1–3% drop on some models.
[07:18] Carlos: depends on model and quantization scheme. for our recommended 4-bit QAT-like profile we generally see negligible quality drop for majority of prompts, but we'll validate on your prompt set. we can also provide a model variant labeled "q-lite" for low-latency.
[07:32] Sofia: also need to confirm whether logs will include any user PII; we want all PII scrambled on ingestion if using hosted fallback.
[07:39] Aisha: yep, we'll ensure scrubbing rules and show an example of masked logs.
[07:44] Carlos: small transcribe note — sometimes the transcript shows "redwood dedicated" as "red wood" — ignore that.
[07:50] Maya: ha noted.
[07:52] Aisha: ok wrapping up, to confirm: Redwood shares runbook v2 + pricing spreadsheet today, Carlos preps canary dashboard and alert rules by monday, QuantaHealth uploads prompt set and success criteria by sunday, and we run dry-run 2026-01-20 9–11am PT. any objections?
[08:13] Eric: none.
[08:14] Maya: good.
[08:15] Sofia: none.
[08:16] Aisha: cool thanks everyone. i'll capture notes and follow up.
